'''Toure' Ahmad Khalid-Murry''' ({{IPAc-en|t|ʊəˈr|eɪ|_|ɑː|ˈ|m|ɑː|d|_|x|ə|ˈ|l|iː|d|_|ˈ|m|ʌr|i}}; born November 8, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is a player development coach for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]].

==College career==
Murry played [[college basketball]] at [[Wichita State University]], leading the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Shockers]] to the second round of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] and winning the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament]]. Murry averaged 12.1 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game during his senior season in 2011–12.

==Professional career==

===2012–13 season===
[[File:Toure Murry Knicks Summer League 2013.jpg|150px|thumb|left|Murry playing for the Knicks in the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]]]
After going undrafted in the 2012 NBA draft, Murry joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the 2012 NBA Summer League. He spent August and September in Turkey and Israel before returning to the United States. On November 2, 2012, he was selected with the 15th overall pick by the [[Austin Toros]] in the [[2012 NBA Development League Draft]]. Three days later, he was traded to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_trade_with_rgv_2012_11_06.html|title=Austin Toros Trade With RGV Vipers For Patrick Sullivan|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=November 5, 2012|work=NBA.com}}</ref> During his rookie season, he played 52 games in total for the Vipers, averaging 9.0 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.8 steals per game.

===2013–14 season===
In July 2013, Murry joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the Orlando Summer League and the New York Knicks for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 11, 2013, he signed with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14235|title=Knicks sign Toure Murry and Chris Smith|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=September 11, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com}}</ref> On January 29, 2014, he was assigned to the Erie BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15145|title=Knicks assign Cole Aldrich, Toure Murry, Jeremy Tyler to D-League|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 29, 2014|work=InsideHoops.com}}</ref> He was recalled the next day. On January 31, 2014, he was reassigned to the BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15154|title=Knicks assign Toure Murry to D-League|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 31, 2014|work=InsideHoops.com}}</ref> He was recalled the next day. In 51 games for the Knicks in 2013–14, he averaged 2.7 points and 1.0 assists per game.

===2014–15 season===
On August 28, 2014, Murry signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-free-agent-toure-murry|title=Jazz Signs Free Agent Toure' Murry|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=August 28, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 13, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-assign-toure-murry-d-leagues-idaho-stampede|title=Jazz Assign Toure' Murry to D-League's Idaho Stampede|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=November 13, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was recalled by the Jazz on December 2,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-recall-toure-murry-idaho-stampede|title=Jazz Recall Toure' Murry from Idaho Stampede|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=December 2, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref> reassigned on December 31,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-assign-toure-murry-d-leagues-idaho-stampede-0|title=Jazz Assign Toure' Murry to D-League's Idaho Stampede|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=December 31, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref> and recalled again on January 3.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-recall-toure-murry-idaho-stampede-0|title=Jazz Recall Toure' Murry from Idaho Stampede|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 3, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> He went on to make his Jazz debut later that night.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150103/UTAMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Burke's hot shooting leads Jazz over Timberwolves|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 3, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> The next day, he was waived by the Jazz<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-toure-murry|title=Jazz Waive Toure' Murry|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 4, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> and on January 10, he was reacquired by the Rio Grande Valley Vipers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4913992|title=Vipers Acquire Toure' Murry|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 10, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com}}</ref> On February 7, 2015, Murry recorded his first career triple-double after posting 10 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in a 109–107 win over the Texas Legends.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021400251/|title=Rio Grande Valley Vipers 109 - Texas Legends 107|publisher=G-League Stats|date=February 7, 2015|access-date=June 8, 2020}}</ref>

On March 12, 2015, Murry signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/03/12/wizards-sign-toure-murry|title=WIZARDS SIGN TOURE' MURRY|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=March 12, 2015|work=MonumentalNetwork.com}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract with the Wizards on March 22<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/03/22/wizards-sign-toure-murry-to-second-10-day-contract|title=WIZARDS SIGN TOURE' MURRY TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=March 22, 2015|work=MonumentalNetwork.com}}</ref> but was released halfway through his contract on March 27,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/03/wizards-release-murry.html|title=Wizards Release Toure' Murry|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=March 27, 2015|work=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref> and returned to the Vipers three days later. He was subsequently deactivated by the Vipers and did not play for the team again in 2014–15.

===2015–16 season===
In July 2015, Murry joined the Washington Wizards for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], but was limited to just two total minutes of action due to a right groin injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_toure_murry/|title=2015 Summer League Player Profile – Toure' Murry|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> He later re-signed with the Wizards on September 25, 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/09/25/wizards-sign-five-for-training-camp|title=Wizards Sign Five for Training Camp|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=September 25, 2015|work=MonumentalNetwork.com|archive-date=September 27, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927204655/http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/09/25/wizards-sign-five-for-training-camp|url-status=dead}}</ref> only to be waived again by the team on October 24 after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/10/24/wizards-waive-five|title=WIZARDS WAIVE FIVE|access-date=October 24, 2015|date=October 24, 2015|work=MonumentalNetwork.com|archive-date=October 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025202356/http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/10/24/wizards-waive-five|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 31, 2015, Murry was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] in a trade with the Vipers.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065516|title=Legends Complete Two Trades, Announce 2015-16 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> On November 13, he made his debut for the Legends in a 104–82 loss to the Austin Spurs, recording 10 points, five rebounds and seven assists in 39 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151113/TEXAUS/|title=Cotton, Spurs Rout Legends as Satnam Singh Debuts|work=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2015|access-date=March 12, 2016|archive-date=January 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119200917/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151113/TEXAUS/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 4, 2016, Murry was traded to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Andre Dawkins]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/skyforce-acquire-toure-murry/n-5107550|title=Skyforce Acquire Toure Murry|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 4, 2016|access-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref> On March 11, he made his debut for the Skyforce in a 121–117 win over the [[Canton Charge]], recording 12 points, three rebounds, four assists and one block in 24 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160311/SXFCTN/|title=Skyforce Drop Charge|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> He helped the Skyforce finish with a D-League-best 40–10 record in 2015–16, and went on to help the team win the league championship with a 2–1 Finals series win over the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]], his second D-League title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|title=Sioux Falls Skyforce Cap Historic Season with First NBA D-League|work=NBA.com|date=April 27, 2016|access-date=April 28, 2016|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428121154/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
In July 2016, Murry joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. On September 26, 2016, he signed with the Timberwolves,<ref>{{cite news|title=TIMBERWOLVES ANNOUNCE 2016-17 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-announce-2016-17-training-camp-roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in three preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES WAIVE BUTLER, MURRY|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-butler-murry|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref> On December 5, he signed with [[Yeşilgiresun Belediye]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/219366/toure-murry-inks-with-yesilgiresun.html|title=Toure Murry inks with Yesilgiresun|work=Sportando.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> On February 3, 2017, he parted ways with Yeşilgiresun.<ref>{{cite news|title=Toure Murry leave Yesilgiresun Belediyespor|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/225093/toure-murry-leave-yesilgiresun-belediyespor.html|access-date=February 3, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=February 3, 2017}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
On July 24, 2017, Murry signed with German club [[ratiopharm Ulm]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=ratiopharm Ulm signs guard Murry|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7yu34gukfpgo9oao|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170727025815/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7yu34gukfpgo9oao|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 27, 2017|access-date=July 24, 2017|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 24, 2017}}</ref> On January 10, 2018, he left Ulm and signed with Greek club [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Toure Murry leaves Ulm to join Promitheas|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/260696/toure-murry-leaves-ulm-to-join-promitheas.html|access-date=January 10, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=January 10, 2018}}</ref>

===2019–20 season===
On July 18, 2019, Murry joined Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica (basketball)|Benfica]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol|Portuguese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|date=18 July 2019|title=Toure' Murry is a new signing|url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/en-us/agora/noticias/2019/07/18/basquetebol-benfica-contratacao-toure-murry-chega-para-a-posicao-de-base|work=S.L. Benfica|access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref> He averaged 10.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game. Murry left the team in January 2020.<ref name="chelidze" />

===2020–21 season===
On September 6, 2020, Murry signed with [[BC Luleå]] of the [[Basketligan]].<ref name="chelidze">{{cite web |last1=Chelidze |first1=Dimitri |title=Toure Murry (ex Benfica) is a second USA added to the roster of BC Lulea |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Sweden/news/643591/Toure-Murry-(ex-Benfica)-is-a-second-USA-added-to-the-roster-of-BC-Lulea |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 7, 2020 |date=September 6, 2020}}</ref>

===2021–22 season===
Murry began the 2021–22 season with Al Qadsia of the [[Kuwaiti Division I Basketball League]]. On January 5, 2022, Murry signed with [[BC Ternopil]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cherkasov |first1=Sergey |title=Ternopil TNEU adds Murry to their roster, ex Qadsia |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Ukraine/news/725057/Ternopil-TNEU-adds-Murry-to-their-roster,-ex-Qadsia |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 5, 2022 |date=January 5, 2022}}</ref> He then joined the [[Astros de Jalisco]] in Mexico, winning a [[CIBACOPA]] league title, before announcing his retirement in September 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.meganoticias.mx/guadalajara/noticia/jugador-de-astros-cibacopa-se-despide-de-su-carrera-profesional/358812|title=Jugador de Astros (CIBACOPA) se despide de su carrera profesional|work=MegaNoticias|first=Darinka|last=Talavera|date=September 9, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article265377616.html|title='No regrets': Former Wichita State star Toure' Murry retires from pro basketball career|work=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|first=Taylor|last=Eldridge|date=September 7, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref>
